reason: The cited evidence shows LCO in CrCoNi (E1) and CoCrNi (E2) alloys, but neither involves stainless steel (which contains Fe and often Mo, Mn, Si), nor do they demonstrate Cr/Ni surface segregation, passive film formation, or corrosion resistance. The key premises about the alloy system, surface segregation, and corrosion mechanism are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Thermal aging at 650°C for 10 hours can induce local chemical ordering (LCO) in Cr-bearing stainless steel.
LCO involves preferential Cr and Ni segregation near the surface.
LCO leads to a uniform, defect-minimized passive oxide film.
LCO suppresses micro-galvanic cells and pitting corrosion.
The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates LCO in relevant alloy systems.
